Nathanael Hardy
nuh-THAN-yel HAR-dee
proper noun
From the surname Hardy (bold, enduring); borne by a London preacher noted for his exposition of the First Epistle of John.

📖 Biblical Definition

Nathanael Hardy was a preacher of London in the seventeenth century, a man of learning and diligence whose chief monument is a large and warm exposition of the First Epistle of John, wherein he opened that Epistle of love and light with pastoral care. Following the apostle, Hardy pressed the great tests of eternal life — that God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all (1Jo 1:5); that the blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanseth us from all sin; that hereby we know that we are of the truth if we love the brethren; and that the beloved of God should not love the world, neither the things that are in the world. He taught assurance not as presumption but as the fruit of obedience and love, for he that keepeth His commandments dwelleth in Him, and God in him. The dictionary honours Hardy as a faithful expositor who fed the church upon the milk and marrow of an apostolic letter, holding forth the incarnate Word made manifest, the propitiation for our sins, and the perfect love that casteth out fear. He would have his hearers know that they had eternal life, that they might believe on the name of the Son of God, and walk in the light as He is in the light.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A London preacher noted for his warm exposition of the First Epistle of John.

expand to see more

NATHANAEL HARDY, a preacher of London in the seventeenth century.

He was a man of learning and pastoral diligence.

His chief monument is an exposition of the First Epistle of John.

He pressed the apostle’s tests of love, light, and obedience.

He taught assurance as the fruit of walking in the light.

📖 Key Scripture

1Jo 1:5 — "This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all."

1Jo 1:7 — "But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin."

1Jo 4:18 — "There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love."

1Jo 5:13 — "These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A faithful expositor, not a contested doctrine; his life recovers the principle of assurance grounded in obedient love.

expand to see more

Hardy is preserved because his exposition of First John holds together what men are ever tempted to divide — the free cleansing of the blood of Christ and the necessary fruit of walking in the light. He pressed the apostle’s tests of true faith, that believers might know they have eternal life without either despairing or presuming.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is assurance grounded in obedient love — that God is light, that the blood of Jesus Christ cleanseth from all sin, and that we know we are of the truth when we love the brethren and keep His commandments. Against a cheap profession that never bears fruit, Hardy insists on the marks; against an anxious legalism, he holds forth the perfect love that casteth out fear. He would have the church walk in the light, as He is in the light, and so have fellowship one with another.
